sample-broken-app.title: Outdated Node.js engine specification (>=8 <14)
sample-broken-app.explanation: The repository declares compatibility with Node.js >=8 <14, which reached End-of-Life. Modern runtimes (Node 20/22 LTS) will trigger deprecation warnings or fail strict engine checks.
sample-broken-app.proposedFix: Update package.json "engines": { "node": ">=20.0.0" } and test build scripts.
sample-broken-app.verification: Run npm or node on current environment to ensure engine constraint passes.

sample-broken-app.title: Deprecated dependency: request (^2.88.2)
sample-broken-app.explanation: request is deprecated. Deprecated in 2020 and unmaintained. Causes memory leaks and lacks modern HTTP/2 support.
sample-broken-app.proposedFix: Replace request with modern alternative: native fetch or undici / axios.
sample-broken-app.verification: Remove request from package.json and verify code compiles without references to request.

sample-broken-app.title: Deprecated new Buffer() constructor in index.js

evidence.snippet: // Bug 2: Deprecated new Buffer() constructor (triggers security & modern node deprecation)

sample-broken-app.explanation: new Buffer() was deprecated in Node.js 6 and poses security risks (uninitialized memory exposure). Use Buffer.from() or Buffer.alloc(). Found in index.js:8.
sample-broken-app.proposedFix: Replace new Buffer(arg) with Buffer.from(arg) for strings/arrays or Buffer.alloc(arg) for sizes.
sample-broken-app.verification: Verify with Node.js runtime execution without DEP0005 deprecation warnings.
